\textbf{A020 --- Selector boundary tests.} Construct selectors with coincident Fourier supports, unequal cell sizes, affine cells, and nearly identical branches. Refute any proposed closure that silently discards interference or selector influence.

\emph{Acceptance tests.} Start from all signed convolution identities and retain the phase signs through the decisive cancellation. Specify the entropy weight and any absolute-convergence/finite-sum manipulation; Parseval or triangle inequality alone must not silently replace the needed signed conclusion. Locate the consequence absent from the fixed-order non-Boolean controls and quantify the paid term on an actual Boolean class.

\textbf{A032 --- Boolean phase realizability.} Given a candidate spectral probability law, determine whether signs can produce a Boolean inverse Walsh transform. Produce exact impossibility certificates or actual truth tables, never a merely normalized vector.

\emph{Acceptance tests.} An accepted realization has inverse Walsh values exactly $\pm$1, not merely norm one or values numerically close to signs. An impossibility claim specifies the complete finite phase domain or a proved algebraic obstruction; a failed heuristic search is labelled inconclusive. Provide the common realizability interface reused by uniform coding, correlated auxiliaries, and the separate biased-normalization referee.
